title: Father of All, in Whom Alone
description: Father of All, in Whom Alone in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 88. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther of all, in whom a-lone We live, and move, and breathe, One bright ce-les-tial ray dart down, And cheer thy sons be-neath.

lines: Father of all, in whom alone
We live, and move, and breathe,
One bright celestial ray dart down,
While in thy word we search for thee,
Open our eyes, and let us see
The light that shines so clear;
And give us ears to hear.
Before us make thy goodness pass,
Which here by faith we know;
Let us in Jesus see thy face,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
